scope: All 47 observations/proposals in five Oct27 reports; 19 work packages plus nine positive observations. Per-task implementation and validation are recorded separately.
rules: Task is a problem or feature. Tested/untested is a separate flag.
Close only implemented scope; partial fixes retain explicit remaining work.
No custom Unreal engine requirement; DSH stays paused.
Test focused changed behavior, actual output/help and visual layout where relevant; reuse existing support-tool evidence.
Archive evidence and update main/dashboard after each bounded accepted batch.
Unknown causes stay investigations; feature proposals are not regressions.

waves.1: Data safety and installation: documentation quick win; quoted literals; engine-write reproduction and supported recovery design.
waves.2: Graph entry correctness, local layout, geometry/report filtering and syntax consistency.
waves.3: Assisted play debugging, logs, explicit activation/console actions and disconnect diagnostics.
waves.4: Custom events, function flags and collapse-to-function capabilities.
waves.5: Per-user individual tool controls and domain presets.

tasks.title: Filter large layout and comment reports
tasks.scope: Layout reports, comment listing and capture selection
tasks.acceptance: Support a bounded node/box/region scope with explicit overlap inclusion rules. Put actionable scoped problems before verbose details and expose truncation/paging. Do not force oversized full-graph capture.
tasks.verification: 390-node/29-box equivalent synthetic graph; scoped overlap and comment remain visible within output budget.
tasks.source_review: Layout report measures full graph and puts boxes/longest wires before findings; final text truncation can hide relevant findings. Findings already carry node IDs. CommentList computes relationships against all boxes but caps output without scoped selection. Capture already supports targeted node/box views; reuse it.
tasks.repair_contract: Extend existing layout report and comment list with optional Scope and bounded Offset/Limit. Scope empty means whole graph; node:<exact ID or unique hex>, box:<exact comment ID or unique hex>, region:x,y,width,height with finite positive dimensions. Strict overlap selects touching rectangles, not mere edge contact; box scope includes the box plus intersecting nodes. Layout findings included when any involved node is selected, retaining external endpoints. Comment scope includes requested/intersecting boxes; compute nesting/overlap against full graph. Put actionable finding records before verbose context. Page complete records with explicit matched/shown/omitted/next offset; state pages are live and restart after edits. Require explicit graph for scoped comments. No silent expansion, arbitrary selection guesses or automatic whole-graph capture. Verify a synthetic 390-node/29-box graph, scoped overlap, comments, caps, invalid scopes and help; inspect targeted screenshot. Existing behavior and no-mutation controls retained.
tasks.implementation_progress: Scoped report implementation, help and dense workflow accepted; explicit oversized-record regression passed.
tasks.resolution: Node/box/region scopes and complete-record paging expose relevant findings before bounded context. Invalid scopes refuse; oversized records stop automatic paging with honest omission and explicit skip guidance. Targeted capture avoids giant graph capture. Failures and measurement limits retained in review.

tasks.repair_contract: Add PreviewTurboMCPCustomEventAdd and EditTurboMCPCustomEventAdd with Asset, GraphName, Name and Inputs. tasks.title: Make play focus and application activation explicit
tasks.acceptance: Distinguish Slate focus from OS foreground activation. Report inactive application honestly; design explicit activation request with verified outcome and fallback when OS refuses. Keep inactive-input guard.
tasks.verification: Inactive/active editor cases, focus outcome readback, activation refusal and no unintended input delivery.
tasks.source_review: Focus currently sets Slate user focus without distinguishing inactive application. Hold correctly rejects inactive Slate state. Stock SWindow supports BringToFront and native IsForegroundWindow; activation requests may be refused or delayed by the OS.
tasks.repair_contract: Extend existing PlayInput Action with explicit activate: resolve the PIE viewport owning window, require empty Key/Value/Seconds and no held input, request stock native activation, report immediate foreground and Slate-active observations without claiming guaranteed success or sending a key. Focus remains Slate-only and says so. Read state includes owning-window foreground separately from application active. Preserve inactive input guard. Help explains activation side effects, delayed/refused fallback, and menu focus preservation. Extend existing CommonPlay workflow with active/inactive state, argument refusal, no-key delivery and live help; record simulated callback controls separately from actual native activation observations. No engine changes or OS focus-policy bypass. Source follow-up: unattended launcher installs FTurboMCPFocusGuard, which returns foreground on activation. Explicit activate must refuse clearly while that guard is active, without silently disabling it. The owned CommonPlay fixture may temporarily remove/reinstall the guard to measure a real stock foreground request; restore it on all exits. Keep callback simulation distinct from OS observations.

integrator_test_scope.reason: Expose existing CommonPlay-only selection with a supervisor-preserved TMCP_COMMON_PLAY_ONLY variable; reuse existing scenario without running unrelated vision workflows. Keep the full default suite unchanged.

tasks.implementation_progress: Implemented explicit activation request, guard refusal, separate native/Slate state and fallback. Native workflow and offline gate passed; OS did not grant foreground in this host run.
tasks.resolution: Implemented the requested activation/focus contract, including refusal and manual fallback. This does not claim successful unattended foreground acquisition: Windows foreground remained no in the observed run. Failure evidence and simulation limits are retained.

tasks.title: Read bounded filtered editor/play logs
tasks.acceptance: Return category/text/time or cursor filtered records with bounded output, timestamps, dropped-count and session identity. Distinguish output log from tool-call log. Avoid arbitrary filesystem read capability.
tasks.verification: Known log markers across cursor boundaries, category/text filters, truncation and stale cursor; clear live help.
tasks.source_review: Only per-call warning capture and tool-call history exist. Neither provides editor log history. Add a bounded output-device history during enabled module lifetime; do not change existing per-call attribution.
tasks.repair_contract: ReadTurboMCPEditorLog reads an enabled-session memory ring of at most 2048 records, at most 2048 characters each. Capture UTC timestamp, category, verbosity, monotonically increasing sequence and session GUID. Optional exact Category, case-insensitive Contains, UTC Since and exclusive Cursor=session:sequence; default empty cursor starts oldest retained. Limit 1..100, character-budget whole records. Return next cursor, retention loss since requested cursor, filtered/scanned counts, message truncation flags and session identity. Refuse malformed/future/other-session cursor and invalid time/limit. Filtered scans advance cursor only through considered records, never skip a matching record that did not fit output. Thread-safe capture, no recursive logging under lock, install only when enabled and detach safely on shutdown. No arbitrary file path, disk log read, clear operation or world attribution claims. Test actual GLog markers, filters, sequential pages, retention loss, truncated text, stale cursor, live help, no self-generated log recursion. Integrator owns catalog/inventory registration.
tasks.resolution: Implemented ReadTurboMCPEditorLog with bounded session history, category/text/time filters, exclusive cursor paging, retention-loss and truncation reporting. Public tool and live help verified in a focused native workflow.

tasks.title: Execute explicitly targeted diagnostic console commands
tasks.scope: Editor versus PIE console target and command-result contract
tasks.acceptance: Define supported diagnostic command surface before implementation. Explicit world target and side-effect description; reject ambiguous targets. Do not treat command dispatch as verified effect or captured output. Confirm risky operations separately.
tasks.verification: Logging/diagnostic command and CVar cases with log/readback evidence; invalid target/command and blocked destructive cases.
tasks.source_review: Stock IConsoleManager exposes registered CVar lookup and world-aware ProcessUserConsoleInput. Log suppression handles Log list/category verbosity through Exec; SlateCore registers SlateDebugger.Event.Start/Stop. Existing TurboMCP has no console execution tool. No engine changes needed.
tasks.repair_contract: Add PreviewTurboMCPDiagnosticConsole and EditTurboMCPDiagnosticConsole. Require Target=editor or pie:<instance>; reject absent, invalid or duplicate world targets. Support Log list [category], Log <exact-existing-category> <verbosity>, SlateDebugger.Event.Start/Stop, and registered CVar queries or single-value assignments. Parse a single bounded command; refuse command chaining, multiline text, arbitrary exec commands, global log changes and destructive commands. CVar writes refuse read-only/unregistered variables and require separate preview plus an exact confirmation token tied to target, command and current value. Log verbosity and debugger changes also require preview confirmation. Preview does not execute. Describe that log, Slate debugger and ordinary CVars affect the process even when a PIE world is selected; do not imply world isolation. Use a bounded output device, label synchronous output, return handled/dispatch status separately from effect verification. CVar readback reports actual before/after and failure to take effect; log category readback reports actual level. Debugger dispatch alone is not proof of event capture: direct the caller to ReadTurboMCPEditorLog. Explain persistent session effects and how to restore prior values. No config save, file access, shell execution or custom engine. Tests cover live help and public calls, exact world selection, stale confirmation, unknown/read-only CVar, malformed/chained/destructive commands, logging and CVar readback, debugger dispatch and subsequent log evidence. Tests restore settings they change. Integrator owns suite/catalog and routing/coverage registration.
tasks.integration_review: The call recorder blocks most Edit tools during PIE. Integrator explicitly permits only EditTurboMCPDiagnosticConsole through that gate; its own target/command/confirmation validation remains mandatory. Public MCP verification during a timed PIE session is required, not direct native calls alone.
tasks.resolution: Implemented preview-confirmed diagnostic console operations with explicit world selection, process-wide effect descriptions, bounded output and actual CVar/log readback. Public MCP dispatch verified in editor and timed PIE.

tasks.repair_contract: Retain no-replay semantics. Add a bounded structured last_failure record and exception diagnostic with UTC time, tool/method, failure type, reconnect success/failure, replay=false and explicit unknown mutation outcome/server cause. Do not store arguments, credentials or raw session IDs. Provide correlation guidance to capture ReadTurboMCPStatus, editor log window and shutdown/crash evidence; disconnected server cause and historical revision remain unknown unless independently observed. Add module lifecycle identity logging using existing stock engine/module APIs (compiler time is not revision proof). Extend real client-control-flow tests for losses before/after effect, failed reconnect, no duplicate write and bounded safe diagnostic fields. Document recurrence collection and state reconciliation. Native startup evidence verifies identity log; no speculative repair of the historical disconnect.
tasks.resolution: Completed incident capture, no-replay regression coverage, startup identity logging and reconnect/state-reconciliation guidance. Investigation result: historical cause is unknown, not repaired by assumption.
